title: Renewals and Scale Readiness Playbook — Enterprise Accounts
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary:

This playbook defines a structured program for (1) assessing enterprise accounts for scale readiness post-launch, (2) detecting renewal risk early, and (3) coordinating cross-functional remediation plans that reduce churn and operational surprises when customer usage grows. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support L2/L3, and Product/Platform stakeholders.

Goals:
- Ensure customers approaching renewal are operating within predictable cost and reliability envelopes.
- Provide a reproducible, score-driven renewal risk assessment that drives action items and engineering prioritization.
- Align scale-readiness remediation to measurable SLO improvements and cost optimizations.

Scope:
- Applies to enterprise customers with Dedicated or Private deployments and mid-market accounts with predictable Hosted usage > $10k/month.
- Excludes one-off POCs under $1k/month; those follow the standard onboarding checklist.

Quick definitions:
- Scale Readiness: Customer’s ability to increase traffic 2–5x without service degradation or >25% token-cost inflation.
- Renewal Risk Score (RRS): Composite score (0–100) combining health, cost, and reliability signals used to categorize accounts: Green (>=75), Yellow (50–74), Red (<50).

Owner and escalation path:
- Playbook owner: Customer Success Operations (CS Ops).
- Day-to-day: Assigned CSM owns customer comms and remediation tracker.
- Technical remediation: Platform SE owns backlog items for runtime/model changes.
- Escalation: For RRS Red, file a Severity-3 cross-functional ticket in JIRA and notify on #cs-urgent with tag @oncall-platform.

Signals and telemetry (inputs to RRS):
1) Service health (40% weight) — SLO adherence for last 30 days:
   - Availability SLO: 99.9% (target), measured per deployment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private).
   - Error budget burn: >10% monthly triggers caution.
   - Latency: P95 < 600ms for short-chat routes (<= 256 tokens), P95 < 900ms for long generation routes (>256 tokens).
   Example PromQL checks:
   - availability_30d = (sum_over_time(up{service="redwood-api"}[30d]) / 30) * 100
   - p95_latency = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/complete"}[30d])) by (le))

2) Cost & efficiency (30% weight) — Monthly token spend trends and per-token cost variance:
   - Warning: month-over-month token spend growth > 40% without matching traffic increase.
   - Cost anomaly query (example):
     SELECT customer_id, sum(token_count * unit_price) AS cost FROM billing.events WHERE month = current_month GROUP BY customer_id

3) Quality / Behavioral signals (20% weight):
   - Eval regressions from baseline prompt-sets (failure rate > 10% on key prompts).
   - Increased rate of human-in-loop corrections or re-roll requests logged with support.

4) Operational readiness (10% weight):
   - Customer has runbook and on-call contacts on file.
   - Backup routing/policy configured (fallback to smaller model family during outages).

Renewal Risk Scoring (calculation):
- Composite RRS = 0.4*H + 0.3*C + 0.2*Q + 0.1*O where H=health_score (0–100), C=cost_score (0–100), Q=quality_score (0–100), O=ops_score (0–100).
- Each sub-score is bucketed: Green (85–100), Amber (60–84), Red (<60).
- Example: A customer with H=78, C=62, Q=90, O=80 => RRS = 0.4*78 + 0.3*62 + 0.2*90 + 0.1*80 = 31.2 + 18.6 + 18 + 8 = 75.8 (Green).

Operational cadence (30/60/90 and renewal cycle):
- Week 0 (Go-Live): Handback call between SE and CSM. Handoff runbook completed and uploaded to customer page in Console.
- 30 days: Initial health check (CSM + SE) using the Scale Readiness Checklist below. Produce an action tracker with owners and ETA.
- 60 days: Progress review; re-score RRS and adjust priority backlog. If RRS drops to Red, trigger an emergency remediation sprint (see Escalation section).
- 90 days: Post-launch optimization (cost/perf) and QBR prep. Recommend scheduling executive QBR 30–60 days prior to renewal.

Scale Readiness Checklist (30-day exam):
1) Traffic profile baseline captured (per-route token distribution).
2) KV cache hit-rate >= 60% for chat workloads that benefit from prefix caching.
3) Autoscaling thresholds validated for 2x expected peak traffic.
4) Quantization profile in use for large model families that support it (int8 or int4 where validated).
5) Fallback routing policy defined for cross-region and model-variant failover.
6) Cost guardrails (per-route budgets) assigned in Console.

Common remediation play types and sample runbooks:
A. Latency spikes under load
   - Quick triage (CSM+SE within 24 hours): check P95/P99, queue lengths, GPU utilization.
   - Runbook steps:
     1) Pull last 2 hours of runtime metrics: `kubectl logs` + `prometheus` queries.
     2) If GPU saturation > 80% on Dedicated, switch to larger instance class or enable burst capacity.
     3) Enable short-term autoscaling policy: min_replicas += 2 for peak windows.
     4) Longer term: introduce batching and KV cache tuning. SE to file RFC for model kernel optimization.

B. Unexpected cost growth
   - Triage (48 hours): identify routes with increased tokens per request, regression in caching, or model family cost differences after model pin updates.
   - Immediate actions:
     1) Apply per-route rate-limits or quota ceilings in Console.
     2) Suggest model quantization and a lower-cost fallback model for non-critical paths.
     3) Recommend prompt engineering changes to cap max_tokens.

C. Quality regressions detected by evals
   - Triage path (7 days): run regression harness from applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks.
   - Steps:
     1) Reproduce failure locally with the same model+params.
     2) If caused by model upgrade, request controlled rollback or canary.
     3) Align with Research to produce micro-adjustment (prompt/template) and ship via rollback/canary.

Escalation matrix and SLAs:
- Yellow RRS: CSM to open action tracker; respond to customer within 48 hours; SE triage within 5 business days.
- Red RRS: Create JIRA P3 (technical) + P0 customer communication ticket; notify platform oncall; target remediation window 72 hours.
- Severity criteria for invoking executive attention: >3 customer-facing incidents in a 30-day window, or projected >20% MRR risk at next renewal.

Action tracker template (one-line per item):
- ID, Owner, Priority (High/Med/Low), Action, Acceptance Criteria, Target Date, Status, Linked JIRA.

Sample API snippet: (used by SEs to produce a usage export for customer)
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/usage/export -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY' -d '{"customer_id":"cust_123","range":"30d","granularity":"daily"}'

QBR content checklist (recommended slide deck sections):
1) Executive summary: SOW, ARR, renewal date, RRS and trend.
2) Operational health: availability, latency, error budget burn, incidents since last QBR.
3) Cost & efficiency: token spend, cost-per-1k-tokens, top routes contributing to spend.
4) Product roadmap: planned infra changes that affect customer performance or cost.
5) Action tracker with owners and progress.
6) Ask: renewal options, reserved capacity proposal, or commitment incentives.

Example renewal conversation triggers and offers:
- For customers with steady usage and RRS Green: propose 12-month reserved capacity discount of 10% with a 3-month early renewal credit.
- For Yellow accounts: offer a 6–9 month commitment with a performance SLA addendum contingent on remediation.
- For Red accounts: avoid renewal offers until remediation succeeds; focus on operational restoration and microscopically defined SLO milestones.

Templates (paste into Salesforce/CRM when logging findings):
- Subject: Post-launch 30-day Readout and Action Items — <Customer>
- Body: Hello <Name>, attached is the 30-day scale readiness report for <Customer>. Key items: RRS=<score>, actions: <list>. Next checkpoint: <date>. Owner: <CSM>.

Appendix A — Example queries and thresholds:
- PromQL: `sum(rate(requests_total{customer_id="cust_123"}[5m])) by (route)` — use to detect sudden traffic shifts.
- SQL: `SELECT route, avg(tokens_per_request) FROM usage WHERE customer_id='cust_123' GROUP BY route` — use to find cost drivers.

Appendix B — Ownership table:
- CSM: primary customer contact, owns action tracker and QBR scheduling.
- Platform SE: runtime tuning, quantization recommendations, and JIRA backlog owner.
- Applied ML: evals and regressions owner.
- Billing: pricing/commitment proposals and reserved capacity contracts.

Appendix C — Example acceptance criteria for successful scale-readiness remediation:
- P95 latency reduced to <700ms across top 3 routes for 7 consecutive days.
- Monthly token spend growth capped at <15% MoM while traffic grows expectedly.
- KV cache hit-rate > 65% for chat workloads where prefix caching applies.

If you have questions or need a template workbook (spreadsheet) for calculating RRS, contact CS Ops (cs-ops@redwood.ai) or open a ticket with the tag `scale-readiness`.
